description: I am participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 with my team and will be working on the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge. I am excited to explore space science, work with NASA data and develop a creative and meaningful solution to the challenge. I plan to complete this project with my team and am not looking for additional team members at this time.
summary:
Every monsoon, persistent cloud cover over 90% blinds traditional optical satellites across Bangladesh right when flood waters expand by kilometers, isolating millions. To solve this, our team created Delta Pulse, an open-source radar remote sensing platform built on 12 calibrated passes of NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band SAR (June–November 2026).
Because NISAR emits 24 cm active microwaves, it sees straight through rain, clouds, and emergent plant canopies. Delta Pulse maps open floodwaters, detects hidden water beneath crops through dihedral double-bounce scattering, tracks river sandbar evolution and groups rice planting cycles without manual field surveys.
The platform translates raw radar files into a zero-install interactive dashboard with real-time audio sonification and Upazila-level exposure numbers, validated with 92% agreement against ESA’s Sentinel-1. It equips relief workers, planners, and farmers with uninterrupted sight during peak monsoon disasters.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

During South Asia's monsoon, optical satellites are essentially blind due to unbroken cloud decks. Delta Pulse overcomes this barrier by harnessing active microwave observations from the NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band SAR (GCOV) mission.

Our system pairs a reproducible, cloud-optimized Python processing pipeline with a lightweight web application. Full NISAR files are over 2 GB each; rather than downloading dozens of gigabytes, our streaming fetcher extracts only the required internal HDF5 spatial chunks via HTTP range requests in about 15 seconds per pass. The pipeline cleans the radar backscatter with a 3×3 variance-preserving Lee filter, converts values to decibels, and classifies inundation into four physical states:

Permanent water bodies (benchmarked by 38-year JRC records),

Newly flooded monsoon waters,

Emergent char sandbars emerging during post-monsoon drainage.

Sub-canopy flooded vegetation, identified through characteristic L-band co-polarized double-bounce scattering.

We then apply unsupervised K-means clustering (𝐾=4) across multi-temporal backscatter trajectories on verified cropland (ESA WorldCover) to track rice growth rhythms (Aman cycle) as fields flood, develop canopy volume scatter, and reach harvest.

Real-World Benefits & Intended Impact:

Zero-Delay Flood Intelligence: When flood crests hit the Jamuna and Haor basins, relief coordinators do not have to wait days for cloudless skies. They can immediately see exact water boundaries.

Actionable Community Exposure: By intersecting active flood masks with 100m UN-adjusted WorldPop counts and official geoBoundaries Upazila borders, we calculate realistic exposed population numbers (reporting explicit ±15% uncertainty bounds) and flooded cropland area for every sub-district.

Independent Scientific Rigor: Our water detection achieves 92.2% overall accuracy when cross-validated pixel-by-pixel against ESA Sentinel-1 C-band radar, and 89.8% against cloud-free Sentinel-2 optical imagery.

Tools, Languages & Software-

Languages & Pipeline: Python 3.12 utilizing earthaccess, asf_search, h5py, fsspec, xarray, rioxarray, rasterio, scikit-learn, scikit-image, geopandas, and matplotlib.

Web Architecture: Zero-build static frontend hosted globally on Vercel using vanilla HTML5, CSS Grid/Flexbox conforming to NASA Research White standards, Leaflet.js, and Chart.js.

Data Sonification: Native Web Audio API synthesis engine running directly in client browsers.

Creative Innovations:

Change Radio (Acoustic Sonification): To make radar physics intuitive and accessible to non-technical users and the visually impaired, we built a real-time sonification engine. At any clicked coordinate or landmark, the 12-pass radar series converts into sound: cross-pol controls pitch on a C-major pentatonic scale (196–659 Hz), the HH−HV ratio shapes harmonic brightness, and newly flooded states trigger a tactile 65 Hz sub-bass pulse with live accessible text captions.

Global Finder: Beyond Bangladesh, the tool connects directly to the live NASA ASF Search API, allowing anyone to draw a box anywhere on the planet (Amazon, Mekong, Mississippi) and generate ready-to-run terminal commands and GeoJSON footprints.

Key Factors & Scientific Caveats Considered:

Data Maturity Hygiene: We strictly quarantined Provisional calibrated science granules from early uncalibrated Beta checkouts to ensure zero artificial sensor drift (<0.25 dB on stable urban targets).

Specular Sandbar Ambiguity: Fresh quartz sandbars (chars) reflect 24 cm radar away like smooth water. Rather than ignoring this physical quirk, we documented it transparently and integrated multi-temporal recession logic to separate dry sandbars from genuine floodwaters.

Unsupervised Crop Hypotheses: We explicitly frame our crop phenology clusters as physical scattering hypotheses rather than claiming a census-grade crop map without ground truth.
